concepts.name: Sets and subsets
concepts.description: A set is a collection of distinct elements; a subset contains only elements that also belong to the original set.

concepts.name: Union, intersection and complement
concepts.description: Union combines elements, intersection keeps only shared elements, and complement takes everything outside a set.

concepts.name: Counting with two sets
concepts.description: |A∪B| = |A| + |B| − |A∩B| avoids double-counting the elements shared by both sets.

concepts.name: Counting with three sets
concepts.description: Extending inclusion-exclusion to three sets requires adding back the triple overlap that gets subtracted too many times.

concepts.name: Counting subsets
concepts.description: A set with n elements has exactly 2ⁿ subsets, including the empty set and the set itself.

formulas.title: Union of two sets
formulas.prompt: How do you find the size of the union of two sets?
formulas.explanation: Adding |A| and |B| counts the shared elements twice, so the overlap is subtracted once to correct for it.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to subtract the intersection, double-counting shared elements.

formulas.title: Complement within a universal set
formulas.prompt: How do you find the size of the complement of a set?
formulas.explanation: The complement is everything in the universal set that is not in A.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting that the complement is relative to the universal set, not some other total.
formulas.applicationPrompt: If the universal set has 20 elements and |A|=8, find |A'|.

formulas.title: Union of three sets
formulas.prompt: How do you find |A ∪ B ∪ C|?
formulas.explanation: Each pairwise overlap is subtracted once, but this removes the triple overlap three times, so it must be added back once.
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting to add back the triple intersection at the end.
formulas.applicationPrompt: Given the sizes of three sets and all their overlaps, find |A∪B∪C|.

formulas.title: Number of subsets
formulas.prompt: How many subsets does a set with n elements have?
formulas.formula:
Number of subsets = 2ⁿ
Number of proper subsets = 2ⁿ − 1
formulas.explanation: Each of the n elements is either in a given subset or not, giving 2 choices per element.
formulas.example: A set with 4 elements has 2⁴ = 16 subsets
formulas.commonMistake: Forgetting that the empty set and the whole set both count as subsets.
formulas.applicationPrompt: How many subsets does a set with 4 elements have?

formulas.title: Set difference
formulas.prompt: How do you find the number of elements in A but not in B?
formulas.explanation: Removing the shared elements from A leaves only the elements unique to A.

formulas.title: Smallest and largest possible overlap
formulas.prompt: Two groups in a fixed total: how small and how large can the overlap be?
formulas.formula:
Largest overlap = the smaller group
Smallest overlap = A + B − Total (or 0 if that is negative)
formulas.explanation: The overlap cannot exceed either group, and the two groups cannot together exceed the total without overlapping.
formulas.example: 100 students, 70 like tea and 60 coffee: both is at least 30 and at most 60.
formulas.commonMistake: Giving one fixed answer when the question only allows a range.
formulas.applicationPrompt: In a class of 50, 35 play cricket and 28 play football. What is the least number who play both?

levels.title: Sets, Unions and Intersections
levels.description: Combining and comparing sets without double-counting shared elements.

blocks.title: Why the union formula subtracts something
blocks.body: If |A|=10 and |B|=6, simply adding gives 16 — but any element in both sets gets counted twice. Subtracting |A∩B| once corrects for that double count.
If two sets share no elements at all, |A∩B| = 0 and the union is just the sum.

levels.title: Set Theory Formulas
levels.description: Union of two and three sets, complement, subset counting, set difference.

levels.title: Direct Set Counting
levels.description: Applying the union formula, complements and subset counts directly.

levels.title: Rearranging and Applying
levels.description: Solving for an unknown region, and word problems with two sets.

questions.question: Set A has 5 elements and set B has 7 elements, and they share no elements. What is |A∪B|?
questions.explanation: Since the sets are disjoint, |A∩B| = 0, so |A∪B| = 5 + 7 − 0 = 12.
questions.method: With no overlap, the union is just the sum.
commonMistakes: Assuming there must always be some overlap to subtract.

questions.question: The formula |A∪B| = |A| + |B| − |A∩B| subtracts the intersection because

options.text: the intersection elements were counted twice
the intersection elements should not be counted at all
the formula only works for disjoint sets

questions.explanation: Adding |A| and |B| counts every element of the overlap twice — once in each set — so subtracting |A∩B| once corrects the double count.
questions.method: Adding two sets over-counts their shared elements.

hints.text: Think about an element that belongs to both A and B.

commonMistakes: Assuming the intersection should not be counted at all.

questions.question: A set has 4 elements. How many subsets does it have (including the empty set and the set itself)?
questions.method: Each element is either in or out of a subset: 2 choices per element.

hints.text: Raise 2 to the power of the number of elements.

questions.question: If |A|=10, |B|=6 and |A∩B|=3, what is |A∪B|?
questions.method: Add the two sets, then subtract the overlap.

hints.text: Do not forget to subtract the intersection.

questions.question: The universal set has 20 elements and |A|=8. What is |A'|?

hints.text: The complement is everything not in A.

questions.question: If |A|=15, |B|=12 and |A∪B|=20, what is |A∩B|?
questions.method: Rearrange the union formula to isolate the intersection.

hints.text: Solve the union formula for |A∩B| instead of |A∪B|.

commonMistakes: Adding |A| and |B| without subtracting the union.

questions.question: If |A|=25 and |A∩B|=9, what is |A−B|?
questions.method: Remove the shared elements from A.

hints.text: A − B keeps only elements unique to A.

questions.question: In a class of 40 students, 25 like Math and 20 like Science, and 10 like both. How many like neither?
questions.method: Find the union first, then subtract from the total.

hints.text: "Neither" is the total minus the union.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to subtract the overlap before finding "neither."

questions.question: A universal set has 50 elements. |A|=18, |B|=22, |A∩B|=7. How many elements are in neither A nor B?
questions.method: Find the union, then take the complement of that within the universal set.

hints.text: "Neither" means outside both A and B.

commonMistakes: Subtracting |A| and |B| separately instead of the union.

questions.question: A set has 6 elements. How many proper subsets does it have?
questions.explanation: Total subsets: 2⁶ = 64. Proper subsets exclude the set itself: 64 − 1 = 63.
questions.method: Subtract 1 from the total subset count to exclude the full set.

hints.text: A proper subset cannot be the whole set itself.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to subtract 1 for the full set.

questions.question: |A|=30, |B|=25, |C|=20, |A∩B|=10, |B∩C|=8, |A∩C|=7, |A∩B∩C|=3. What is |A∪B∪C|?
questions.method: Sum the sets, subtract pairwise overlaps, then add back the triple overlap.

hints.text: Do not forget to add the triple intersection back at the end.

questions.question: In a survey of 100 people: 50 read A, 40 read B, 30 read C, 20 read A&B, 15 read B&C, 10 read A&C, and 5 read all three. How many read none of the three?
questions.method: Find the union using inclusion-exclusion, then subtract from the total.

hints.text: "None" is the total minus the three-set union.

commonMistakes: Forgetting to add back the triple overlap before subtracting from the total.

questions.question: A set has n elements and 128 subsets. What is n?
commonMistakes: Guessing n from 128 ÷ 2 instead of using powers.
